status: started 2026-09-27 by the test author at the owner's request, after the swim-fatigue rule broke the Dive rung and nothing caught it; reviewed by humans, enforced by tests/test_system_contracts.py
rule: A contract is one system's guarantee that another system relies on. A change to any system's rule runs `python -m pytest tests/test_system_contracts.py`; a new assumption one system makes about another gets a contract here and a test there (.claude/rules/testing.md 'Cross-system contracts').

fields.owner: the system whose data or code provides the guarantee
fields.consumers: the systems that rely on it; at least one differs from the owner
fields.constrained_by: systems that do not rely on the guarantee but can break it with a change of their own
fields.stated_in: where the guarantee is written: path:line and a quote the line must still contain
fields.tests: the tests that enforce it (path::function); tests in tests/test_system_contracts.py are named test_contract_*
fields.fails_today: cases (pytest ids, fnmatch patterns) that fail on the recorded commit, each with its reason; the tests mark them strict xfail, so a fix makes the run fail until the entry is removed

contracts.title: Dive is unlimited underwater
contracts.statement: A Dive-trained player with a Dive-capable Pokemon in the party, eyes at the ladder's depth, can stay under water for at least ten minutes without being hurt or knocked out by any system: the air ladder and swim fatigue together.

stated_in.quote: An unlocked Dive ability plus a qualifying Pokemon gives unlimited
Keep air full while submerged
| **Dive** (training after gym 6, with a Dive-capable Pokemon) | unlimited |
new rule is **knocked out at 33 s**

contracts.title: Surf gives its whole bonus at depth, and nothing hurts a Surf player sooner than the ladder does
contracts.statement: A Surf-trained player with a Surf-capable Pokemon in the party, at depth, has air held full for surf_bonus_ticks per submersion, then vanilla's 300 ticks, before any hit; no other system hurts or knocks them out sooner than the ladder alone does.

stated_in.quote: 10. An unlocked Surf ability plus a qualifying Pokemon in the active party gives
Hold vanilla air full for 900 bonus ticks, then allow the normal 300 ticks: about 60 seconds total
45 s held full, then vanilla 15 s, then the same two hits: about 61 s

cases.sound_ferry_from_the_jetty: Its `to` end, (7210, 6960), is recorded as "the town square's centre (data/placements.json settlements.sea_town)". Measured tonight with tools/ground.py through ground.for_settlement('sea_town') (kind sea_deck, deck level y62, 8,149 deck cells): that column is ground y55, seven blocks under a sea of y62, and it is NOT one of the deck cells. The sea town has moved out from under the crossing. data/ferries.json agrees and is the evidence: BOTH stops of the sound_ferry line, `pacifidlog_jetty` and `pacifidlog_square`, are status "retired", and `pacifidlog_south_jetty` is "planned" near (5160, 6658) as "the landing of the new mainland jetty". So this contract measures the swimmability of a strait whose ferry no longer runs, between two ends one of which is open water. NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately: re-pointing it means choosing which line replaces the Sound ferry and where Pacifidlog's square now is, and `pacifidlog_ferry`'s own second stop `pacifidlog_square` is itself retired, so the ferry data is mid-migration. That is the water system's decision, not a passing repair at 3am. The fix is to re-measure both ends against the current sea town and the live line, or to retire the crossing with the line; either removes this entry.

contracts.title: No world pack places a spawn condition its place is not whitelisted for
contracts.statement: Every block a generator's allowed or named list holds (and every block an earthwork places) is either named by no loaded spawn condition, or allowed by a data/spawn_block_policy.json entry whose scope names that place.

stated_in.quote: Spawn-neutral by default.
A template that contains one decides encounters wherever it is placed

contracts.title: A blackout's money charge is flat, so saving is never punished
contracts.statement: A blackout costs a flat amount of money that does not depend on what the player has saved: ceil(money.cap * money.percent / 100) from data/blackout.json, $600 at the recorded values, the same at badge 0 and after the Champion. Nothing in the charge path multiplies, divides or scales the amount by the balance; the balance is read only to keep the charge inside it, so the charge is never more than the player holds, never negative, and a balance above zero always loses at least 1. Therefore the ladder and the markets may price any rung at any amount, however large, without raising the cost of a death: saving for a 20,000 purchase costs $600 a blackout, not 4,000, and a rung's price may change with no change here. Decision B10 (the owner, 2026-10-01), which replaced 20% of the whole balance -- a charge whose expected cost grew with how long the player saved (docs/research/INCOME_MEASUREMENT.md 4.3.3). The charge does not scale with progress by design; the penalties that do are the item claim and the return to a checkpoint, which belong to recovery_claims and blackout_checkpoints.

The test does not exist yet, so tests/test_system_contracts.py::test_every_contract_names_existing_tests fails on this commit until it is written; the entry is not to be deleted to make the suite green. What the test must assert, against the GENERATED pack rather than against data/blackout.json's own arithmetic: (1) run blackout/charge in the simulator at a spread of balances across the cap (1, 199, 599, 600, 601, 3000, 20000, 250000, 2147483647) and assert bo.lost == min(balance, ceil(cap * percent / 100)) every time; (2) assert the charge is strictly flat, i.e. bo.lost is identical at any two balances above the cap, however far apart; (3) assert it never exceeds the balance and is never negative, including balance 0 (nothing charged, charge_calc not called) and balance 1 (exactly 1 charged); (4) prove independence by mutating the GENERATOR, not the data (CLAUDE.md 'How to prove an audit is independent'): re-derive the amount from money.cap and money.percent as read from data/blackout.json, assert it equals the #charge constant the pack sets at load, then change charge_amount() in tools/blackout_pack.py -- drop the ceiling, or put a balance term back -- and assert the test fails; (5) the consumer half: assert the charge path reads no price and no balance-derived scale at all, so no rung in docs/mechanics/PROGRESSION_LADDER.md and no entry in data/traders.json can change what a death costs.
